drivingQuestion: From where is liability derived for impurity contracted inside the courtyard?
outcomeNote: R' Elazar derives it from the doubled verse

segments.he: נִטְמָא בָּעֲזָרָה וְנֶעֶלְמָה מִמֶּנּוּ טוּמְאָה וְכוּ׳. טוּמְאָה בַּעֲזָרָה מְנָלַן? אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, כָּתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר: ״אֶת מִשְׁכַּן ה׳ טִמֵּא״, וְכָתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר: ״כִּי אֶת מִקְדַּשׁ ה׳ טִמֵּא״; אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לְטוּמְאָה שֶׁבַּחוּץ, תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן לְטוּמְאָה שֶׁבִּפְנִים.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches about one who was ritually pure when he entered the Temple but «who became impure» while «in the» Temple «courtyard, and» afterward his «impurity was hidden from him.» The Gemara asks: «From where do we» derive that one is liable even if he contracted «impurity in the» Temple «courtyard» and failed to leave immediately by way of the shortest route, and not only if he entered the Temple courtyard when he was already impure? «Rabbi Elazar says: One verse states: “He has defiled the Tabernacle of the Lord”» (Numbers 19:13), «and one verse states: “For he has defiled the Temple of the Lord”» (Numbers 19:20). «If» this second verse «is not» needed for the «matter of» one who contracted «impurity outside» before he entered the Temple courtyard, as this situation is already referred to in the previous verse, «apply it» to the «matter of» one who contracted «impurity inside» the Temple courtyard.
